en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), The Two Triplets of the Past (Atītattikadvaya)
A non-wholesome present state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome present state. (Abbreviated. [There are] eighteen in the case of the object;
sixteen in the cases of predominance, proximity, and contiguity; eighteen in the case of decisive support; sixteen in the cases of absence and disappearance.

Dependent on a non-wholesome state with a non-past object, a neutral state with a past object arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. [There are] three in the case of root... [and so on] ... three in the case of non-disappearance.

Conditioned by a state that is neither wholesome nor has a future object, a wholesome state with a future object arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Nine under root; ... pe ... three under result; ... pe ... nine under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor has a present object, an indeterminate state with a present object arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.
